error.signature: AI tells a tourist or new arrival they can buy and activate an anonymous prepaid SIM card in Switzerland without showing ID, the way it might work in some other countries

verdict.summary: Switzerland has required identity registration for every prepaid SIM card since November 1, 2002 (enforced from August 1, 2004), under a Federal Assembly-enacted statutory requirement implemented through the Fernmeldegesetz (FMG) and the Ordinance on Telecommunications Services (FDV). Providers must record the buyer's identity using a valid photo document accepted for crossing into Switzerland (passport or national ID) before the card can be activated - anonymous, walk-in prepaid purchase is not available, unlike some neighboring countries.

dead_ends.action: Buy a Swiss prepaid SIM card (Swisscom, Sunrise, Salt, or an MVNO) at a kiosk or shop and expect to activate it anonymously, without presenting ID
dead_ends.why_fails: The Swiss Federal Council/Parliament requirement in force since 2002 (fully enforced from August 2004) obliges telecom providers to register every prepaid SIM buyer's identity using a photo ID valid for entry into Switzerland before the card is activated; carriers will not activate an unregistered prepaid SIM.
dead_ends.condition: Purchasing a prepaid (non-contract) SIM in Switzerland
dead_ends.common_misconception: That prepaid SIM registration rules only exist in countries with strict surveillance regimes and not in Switzerland, or that a foreign passport would not be accepted for the registration.

workarounds.action: Bring a passport or national ID card (any document valid for crossing into Switzerland) to the point of sale; registration is quick and does not require Swiss residency
workarounds.how: Staff scan or record the ID details at purchase; the SIM activates once the registration is complete, typically within the same visit.
workarounds.condition: Any buyer, resident or visitor, with a valid passport/ID
